title: Pleasing the audience and a second-line band photo
summary: Agreeing that audiences like melody and dancing, he says a player must please the public; then points out Johnny Wiggs and Larry Shields in a photo.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Well I think the kids today like to hear melody. I think people still like melody and they like to dance.

I think so. They like to dance. Now I've played for a lot of teenagers already. And they've often told us that they like the band. Because we played a lot of stuff that they heard. And they knew about it, you know. And they like to hear that of course. There's a lot of them that we go out and play these days. They ask you to play rock and roll western. So you've got to learn how to play a little bit of everything. In order to satisfy the public these days. It's the way that I've been doing. If somebody wants me to play a samba, I'm gonna play a samba. I'm gonna play the samba that I know. The one that I can play. And I say that's the main thing about playing music for the public. Is to please the public. Try to play what they want you to play. Not play what you want. I see your friend here, Johnny Wiggs is in this picture here. This is our band there. Larry Shields too. Abby Brunus. Buegman Sam. This is Larry Shields here. Yeah, Larry Shields. This is a picture that was taken some time back in the second line. Connie, I wanted to ask you.
